findings.reason: the plan would gain a reuse map naming velocity.plan_census and roadmap._progress (and why the live inventory is used instead of the git-history census), which is exactly the section a first implementation node needs.
findings.text: §3 proposes a new pending-plan census plus an impl ranking with no reuse search naming what already does both; the velocity view §3 depends on already reports a per-project pending count, and roadmap already derives each plan's impl

findings.reason: forcing the author either to extend the census owner or to state why a separate check is required changes what the plan tells the implementation node to build.
findings.text: the cap is a thin policy layer over the existing pending census, and the section never says why the census cannot be extended to answer "is this project over its limit" instead of a parallel check at creation

findings.reason: naming the owner lets the author extend plan_census (or expose a lightweight live-inventory variant for the create path) rather than fork a second pending census that can drift from the one the velocity gate reports.
findings.text: §3 re-derives the pending census (`_pending_plans`/`_plans_nearest_to_closing`, reckon/mcp.py:3273 and :3294) rather than extending the owner `plan_census`, whose CLOSED_STATUSES + archive definition §1 explicitly adopts, and duplicates the impl reader already owned by reckon/roadmap.py:99 `_progress`

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one config key `pending_plan_limit` drives a single create-path policy in reckon/mcp.py, and the census, the impl ranking and the warning composition are hidden behind one interface rather than exposed as new public surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 re-implements a pending-plan census and impl-progress ranking rather than extending the owners, reckon/velocity.py:409 `plan_census` (whose CLOSED_STATUSES + archive definition §1 itself adopts) and reckon/roadmap.py:99 `_progress`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §3 adds no public definition, CLI option, MCP view or refusal family (the cap check is four module-private helpers in reckon/mcp.py) and, when it relocked to warn mode, retired the refuse-with-override refusal surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 adds a per-project pending-plan census and an impl ranking without searching for, or citing, the mechanisms that already produce both (reckon/velocity.py plan_census, reckon/roadmap.py _progress).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 lays a thin cap/warn policy over the existing pending-plan census without saying why that census cannot carry the check at creation, which is the honest place to extend it.
